methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: ODU and Google launch AI incubator to boost innovation in Hampton Roads - MSN
signals.signal_reading: ODU-Google AI incubator concentrates deep technical capacity in Hampton Roads metro hub, but partnership model could enable knowledge transfer if incubator graduates seed capabilities regionally rather than concentrating talent extraction toward NoVA.

signals.title: New partnership between VCU and AI Ready RVA aims to boost AI education, innovation and community impact - VCU News
signals.signal_reading: VCU's AI Ready RVA partnership explicitly targets community-wide AI education and impact beyond elite institutions, signaling potential for distributed fluency building through peer networks if implementation reaches beyond university walls into workforce ecosystems.

signals.title: Healthcare providers say AI helps them focus on patients. But it also raises questions about privacy, security and the role of humans in medicine
signals.signal_reading: Four-in-five doctors using AI for note-taking and communications indicates rapid platform-delivered adoption creating broad but shallow capability—users consume AI tools without building underlying technical fluency, especially critical in historically underserved regions.

signals.title: Problem-solvers by nature: How Virginia Beach Fire put AI to work - FireRescue1
signals.signal_reading: Virginia Beach Fire Department proactively implementing AI solutions demonstrates distributed problem-solving capacity beyond traditional tech hubs, suggesting deep fluency can emerge through peer-driven adoption when organizations tackle domain-specific challenges.

signals.title: AI pressure grows on Richmond's young workforce - Axios
signals.signal_reading: AI creating pressure on Richmond's young workforce without accompanying evidence of systematic upskilling infrastructure signals risk of shallow, anxious awareness without depth—workers feel disruption but lack pathways to capability building.
